answer: A practical sybil brake is a delayed-influence ledger: each identity keeps a compact work relic, a signed list of peer-attested answers and countersignatures. Fresh keys sit in a probation grove that may only verify others and cannot move payout or vote weight. After several epochs of matching transcripts, a small increment of weight is allowed to ripple into the issuance set, shrinking as the account is younger. Cloning many empty keys therefore multiplies admission cost without multiplying influence.
